name: Maple Preview
tagline: A 20B ternary MoE in 5.31GB, doing 218 tok/s on a Mac mini
description: Deepgrove's 20B-total / 1B-active mixture-of-experts built on ternary weights from the ground up: 24 layers, 256 experts with 8 active, a 3:1 SWA-512-to-global attention mix, and 131K context — a 5.31GB checkpoint that streams 218 tok/s on an M4 Mac mini through Deepgrove's mlx-lm fork, with a Triton/FlashAttention Transformers path for CUDA.
why: Bonsai proved you can crush a trained model down to ternary after the fact; Maple is the other bet — train ternary natively and let the MoE routing pay the quality bill. The card claims reasoning parity with its weight class on LCBv6, AIME 2026, HMMT 2026, and GPQA-D, and the whole thing is MIT with a LICENSE file in the repo.
useCases: Fast local reasoning on Apple Silicon without a discrete GPU
Offline assistants where a 5GB footprint is the budget
Research on native ternary training and low-bit MoE routing
audience: Local-AI tinkerers, Apple Silicon users, quantization researchers

setup.requirements: ~6GB free memory; Apple Silicon via the mlx-lm-deepgrove fork, or CUDA with Triton and FlashAttention. Community GGUFs are appearing

license.code: MIT (Deepgrove's mlx-lm fork and HF repo materials)
license.notes: The HF repo is tagged MIT and — unlike too many model repos we check — ships a standalone LICENSE file, linked from the card itself. No acceptable-use policy, no scale triggers, no riders found. Checked 2026-08-10.

tally.stars: ~275 HF likes, ~1.1k downloads in week one

limitations: It's a preview with minimal agentic post-training and only small-scale RL, the benchmark claims are the card's own with no independent numbers yet, and Deepgrove is a young outfit — treat the quality story as promising, not proven.
take: Bonsai compresses a big model into a phone. Maple asks the sharper question: what if it was never big to begin with?
